step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram represents 3M's serverless modeling platform used by scientists and engineers to publish and execute machine learning and physics-based models. 1. Client web requests enter via CloudFront (Node 0) for edge authentication (with Lambda@Edge). 2. CloudFront serves the single-page application (SPA) static files hosted on S3 (Node 1) and routes API requests to API Gateway (Node 2). 3. API Gateway forwards requests to the serverless container backend running on ECS Fargate (Node 3). 4. ECS manages configuration and access control via DynamoDB (Node 4), reads/writes model artifacts in S3 (Node 1), and initiates compute jobs on the HPC EC2 cluster (Node 6). 5. CI/CD workflow is managed by Step Functions (Node 5), which updates model metadata in DynamoDB (Node 4) and deploys execution files to the HPC EC2 cluster (Node 6). 6. Upon completing execution, the EC2 HPC cluster stores output results directly in S3 (Node 1).

graph.name: 3M Serverless Modeling Platform Architecture
graph.notes: 3M's web application platform for publishing and running machine learning and physics-based HPC models built on serverless AWS services and EC2 HPC clusters.

nodes.name: CloudFront
nodes.notes: Handles entry traffic and edge authentication integrated with a third-party identity provider via Lambda@Edge.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Hosts single-page application assets (HTML/JS) and stores input/output model result files.

nodes.name: API Gateway
nodes.notes: Provides additional authorization and fronts the application backend API layer.

nodes.name: ECS
nodes.notes: Serverless Fargate container layer backing the web application API and managing job execution.

nodes.name: DynamoDB
nodes.notes: Stores configuration data for the frontend and access management settings.

nodes.name: Step Functions
nodes.notes: Orchestrates CI/CD deployment pipelines using Lambda functions when scientists publish new models.

nodes.name: EC2
nodes.notes: High-Performance Computing (HPC) cluster running physics and machine learning model computations.

edges.notes: User authenticates through CloudFront and downloads single-page web app assets from S3.
Authenticated web application calls API endpoints routed through CloudFront to API Gateway.
API Gateway authorizes and forwards requests to ECS Fargate service layer.
ECS queries DynamoDB for frontend configuration and access rights.
ECS retrieves or uploads application resources and model files stored in S3.
ECS instantiates model execution jobs on the EC2 HPC cluster.
Step Functions pipeline writes publishing definitions to DynamoDB.
Step Functions publishes model files and deployment configurations to the EC2 HPC cluster.
EC2 HPC cluster writes computed job output results directly to S3.
